note: DualShock 2 works on PS1, but pressure-sensitive face buttons behave as digital. A few games lose analog support entirely.
Original GameCube controllers work in the Wii's four GC ports for GameCube games and select Wii titles (Smash Bros Brawl).
GameCube memory cards work in the Wii's GC memory card slot, but transferring saves to/from the Wii's internal memory requires the official save-transfer tool.
Original SNES controllers work on the original hardware. For SNES Classic / Mini hardware, use a dedicated adapter.
PAL N64 consoles do not output S-Video on the standard multi-out. Use composite or an internal RGB mod.
PAL SCART cables do not pass video correctly on NTSC consoles without a sync converter.
WaveBird wireless receivers cannot be daisy-chained behind an extension cable — interference and power issues.
Component cables require a GameCube with the digital A/V port (early launch units only). Later DOL-101 boards omitted the port entirely.
Saturn controllers work on a Genesis using the same DB-9 pinout, but the START button maps to MODE on some games.
Dreamcast VGA adapters work in ~80% of titles. The remaining games (Resident Evil Code: Veronica, House of the Dead 2) only output to TV-mode signals.
8BitDo SNES receiver works with most modern Bluetooth controllers. Latency is acceptable for most genres; not recommended for pixel-precise speedruns.
Component cables work with PS2 titles set to progressive scan. PS1 games via backwards compatibility only output interlaced over component.
